claims.text: 10 U.S.C. 176 provides that 'There is in the Department of Defense an Institute to be known as the Armed Forces Institute of Pathology', a joint entity of the three military departments subject to the authority, direction and control of the Secretary of Defense, added by Pub. L. 94-361, title VIII, section 811(b), 14 July 1976, 90 Stat. 933.

claims.source: 10 U.S.C. 176, Office of Law Revision Counsel, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title10-section176&num=0&edition=prelim
claims.text: The Office of Law Revision Counsel serves 10 U.S.C. 176 with the statement 'Text contains those laws in effect on September 1, 2026', so the section creating the Institute remains in force after the Institute itself was disestablished.

claims.source: 2005 Defense Base Closure and Realignment Commission Report, Volume 1, DTIC AD-A466177, OCR text layer, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA466177/DTIC_ADA466177_djvu.txt
claims.text: The 2005 Defense Base Closure and Realignment Commission's final report of 8 September 2005, recommendation 169 (Med 4) on Walter Reed Army Medical Center, directs the Department to 'disestablish all elements of the Armed Forces Institute of Pathology except the National Medical Museum and the Tissue Repository', with the Commission's amended version adding that AFIP capabilities not specified 'will be absorbed into other DoD, Federal, or civilian facilities, as necessary'.

claims.source: 2005 Defense Base Closure and Realignment Commission Report, Volume 1, DTIC AD-A466177, OCR text layer, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA466177/DTIC_ADA466177_djvu.txt
claims.text: The same report records that the Commission found the Department 'failed to sufficiently address several AFIP functions, such as the Radiologic Pathology program, with the associated tissue repository, veterinary pathology and continuing medical education', and that the Secretary of Defense 'deviated substantially from final selection criteria 1, as well as from the Force Structure Plan'.

claims.source: Statutory note 'Establishment of Joint Pathology Center' to 10 U.S.C. 176, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title10-section176&num=0&edition=prelim
claims.text: Pub. L. 110-181, division A, title VII, section 722, 28 January 2008, 122 Stat. 199, provides that 'The President shall establish and maintain a Joint Pathology Center that shall function as the reference center in pathology for the Federal Government', established in the Department of Defense consistent with the 2005 BRAC recommendations, and providing for maintenance and continued modernization of the Tissue Repository.

desc: A Department of Defense pathology institute created by statute in 1976 as a joint entity of the three military departments, with a lineage the 2005 BRAC Commission traces to the Army Medical Museum of 1862. The 2005 BRAC recommendation on Walter Reed disestablished all of its elements except the National Medical Museum and the Tissue Repository, and directed that its unspecified capabilities be absorbed into other DoD, Federal or civilian facilities; Congress then required a Joint Pathology Center in the FY2008 National Defense Authorization Act. Its authorising statute, 10 U.S.C. 176, was never repealed and remains in force. It is drafted here for that documented custody chain over a national tissue repository, not for the claim that put it into the corpus.
